questions.question: What requirement follows for planning delivery of approved relief information through local radio?
questions.expected_answer: Obtain the operating status and broadcast frequencies of commercial stations on the affected islands, together with usable coverage and access for approved public information. Coordinate with Japanese authorities and Embassy channels before selecting broadcasts, retaining another available channel if radio reach is inadequate.

criteria.text: Requests current operating status of commercial radio stations.
Requests the broadcast frequencies needed for the proposed information service.
Relates coverage/access to practical delivery of relief information.
Preserves Japanese coordination and required approvals.

acceptable_alternatives: A named staff information request with no invented station/frequency is acceptable.
error_conditions: Broadcasts independently of the stipulated approvals.
questions.derivation_note: Derives a practical communications information requirement for executing the approved relief-information function.

questions.title: ARG readiness requirement
questions.question: What friendly-force information requirement is needed to support allocation of the ARG/31st MEU to relief?
questions.expected_answer: Track current ARG/31st MEU readiness, availability and relief commitment against its continuing role as the sole afloat crisis-response force. Report a material loss of ability to meet that role for higher-headquarters allocation decisions, without inventing a readiness threshold or assuming relief of standing tasks.

criteria.text: Requests current ARG/31st MEU readiness.
Requests current ARG/31st MEU availability.
Relates relief commitment to the sole afloat crisis-response responsibility.
Links material conflict to higher-headquarters allocation decisions.

acceptable_alternatives: An explicit FFIR or equivalent decision-linked readiness report is acceptable.
error_conditions: Assumes a second ARG can absorb the standing mission.
questions.derivation_note: Derives a decision-linked readiness information requirement from the shared-force trade.

questions.title: Force-commitment comparison criterion
questions.question: What criterion should be added when comparing relief options that use the forward amphibious force?
questions.expected_answer: Compare the loss of remaining crisis-response availability and standing-mission coverage caused by each option, alongside its validated relief benefit. Require current commitments and readiness to support the comparison, and surface conflicts for national/theater prioritisation rather than assuming a free force pool.

criteria.text: Defines the criterion in terms of retained response availability or standing-mission coverage.
Relates that criterion to the relief benefit being compared.
Requires actual readiness/commitment information rather than invented scores.

acceptable_alternatives: Availability duration, committed capability or qualified qualitative risk can operationalise the criterion if sourced.
error_conditions: Rates greater force commitment as automatically better.
questions.derivation_note: Moves from a recognised resource trade to a concrete COA-comparison requirement.

questions.title: Sustainment comparison criterion
questions.question: What sustainment criterion should govern comparison of proposed relief-force packages?
questions.expected_answer: Compare each package’s validated task demand and duration with confirmed US resources and agreed ACSA support, recording any unresolved RFF dependency. A package should not be treated as sustainable merely because its initial force is supportable or an augmentation has been requested.

criteria.text: Defines a demand-versus-confirmed-support comparison.
Includes the duration or scale of the proposed package.
Explicitly records dependence on unapproved augmentation.

acceptable_alternatives: A supportability gate or qualitative comparison with an auditable resource basis is acceptable.
error_conditions: Counts unconfirmed cross-servicing or pending RFF as assured capacity.
questions.derivation_note: Derives an evaluable supportability criterion from the expansion mismatch.

questions.title: Timely relief comparison criterion
questions.question: What delivery criterion should be used to compare relief options against the mission purpose?
questions.expected_answer: Compare time to verified receipt and usability of priority relief at the intended destination for validated needs, rather than time to dispatch or arrival at the staging base alone. State the needed handling, distribution and service-restoration dependencies, without inventing deadlines or quantities.

criteria.text: Defines speed to intended-recipient receipt/usability.
Ties comparison to validated priority relief needs.
Includes material handling/distribution dependencies.

acceptable_alternatives: Time to meet a validated service gap or verified delivery milestone is acceptable.
error_conditions: Uses sortie count alone as a measure of timely relief achieved.
questions.derivation_note: Makes rapid delivery assessable at the intended relief outcome rather than the transport activity alone.

questions.title: Function-specific transition criterion
questions.question: What transition criterion should be included when comparing relief-integrity support options?
questions.expected_answer: Compare how soon and under what verified conditions Japanese authorities and civilian/commercial systems can maintain the supported relief-flow and accountability function without the US contribution. Use a function-specific handover check, maintaining authorized assistance or an agreed continuity arrangement while the validated gap remains.

criteria.text: Defines transition by independently sustained Japanese/civilian function.
Includes relief-flow integrity/accountability, not only elapsed time.
Requires verified gap closure before removing the relevant US support.

acceptable_alternatives: A staged transfer-readiness criterion is acceptable.
error_conditions: Withdraws solely because a preset number of days has elapsed.
questions.derivation_note: Derives a concrete comparison and handover requirement from end-state and function-specific readiness.

questions.title: LOTS support prerequisites
questions.question: What staff action should precede committing to an expanded LOTS delivery schedule?
questions.expected_answer: Validate connector and sealift/fuel capacity against the required flow and expected operating windows, establish what the currently confirmed resources can deliver, and route remaining augmentation needs through RFF validation. Prepare a revised timing or delivery option if the sea window or support fails. Do not claim the pending MSC request already fills the gap.

criteria.text: Requires confirmation of delivery capacity before promising expanded throughput.
Requires verification of the relevant operating window.
Separates confirmed resources from pending augmentation.
Provides a contingent adjustment of timing/route/mode if support or weather is inadequate.

acceptable_alternatives: Phasing deliveries, prioritising validated critical loads or an authority-approved alternative mode can qualify; no particular invented asset is mandatory.
error_conditions: Specifies unsupported daily tonnage or directs unallocated assets.
questions.derivation_note: Converts combined physical and resource constraints into support checks and an executable planning contingency, not just risk reporting.

questions.title: MDA support release gate
questions.question: What coordination action follows before scheduling US sensing and track-sharing support to the JCG?
questions.expected_answer: Check the JCG request and State concurrence against the requested sensing/track-sharing window and actual asset availability. If either condition remains unresolved, keep that support commitment pending, obtain the decision through the responsible coordination channels, and revise or revalidate the support window if the delay changes resource availability. Retain enforcement with Japanese authorities; one approval cannot replace the other.

criteria.text: Checks the JCG request for the proposed support.
Checks Department of State concurrence for the proposed support.
Keeps the support commitment pending while a required condition is unresolved.
Revalidates the support window and resources when approval delay affects availability.
Preserves Japanese enforcement responsibility.

acceptable_alternatives: A release checklist or approval-status board with named institutional owners is acceptable.
error_conditions: Allows one approval to substitute for the other.
questions.derivation_note: The dual approval condition is already supplied by D07:140. The added consequence is commitment control and revalidation of the resource/window coupling if either prerequisite is delayed.

questions.title: Diversion verification task
questions.question: What concrete information and coordination task should resolve the relief-diversion question?
questions.expected_answer: Reconcile dispatch and receipt by shipment, commodity, destination and reporting time with Japanese logistics and law-enforcement liaison. Check recording lag and storm disruption before characterising a loss. If a discrepancy remains, record its location and amount and distinguish an unexplained discrepancy from diversion supported by additional corroboration. Feed supported findings to Japanese authorities for their action and use the discrepancy record to adjust relief accountability.

criteria.text: Requires matched shipment-level dispatch and receipt records.
Identifies the location of any residual discrepancy without inventing it.
Identifies the amount of any residual discrepancy without inventing it.
Checks recording lag as an alternative explanation.
Checks storm disruption as an alternative explanation.
Distinguishes an unresolved discrepancy from corroborated criminal diversion.
Refers supported criminal findings to Japanese authorities.
Uses the record to correct or improve relief accountability.

acceptable_alternatives: A request establishing whether, where and how much loss remains, paired with records reconciliation and Japanese liaison, is acceptable.
A finding of recording lag, accidental loss or unresolved cause is acceptable when supported; diversion is not a compulsory result.
error_conditions: Commands US seizure or declares diversion where only a reporting gap exists.
questions.derivation_note: The packet supplies low-confidence discrepancies and alternative explanations. Reconciliation is a concrete verification task, but a residual unmatched quantity does not by itself establish criminal causation.

questions.title: Assumption-change response
questions.question: What staff response is required when a monitored support assumption is no longer supported?
questions.expected_answer: Identify the affected task and assumption, obtain updated Japanese/interagency confirmation, and hold or revise the affected commitment until its basis is restored or competent authority changes it. Reassess protection for changed threat behaviour and report mission/force expansion through the specified chain. Do not treat assumption failure as new authority.

criteria.text: Identifies the task affected by the challenged assumption.
Obtains updated confirmation from the responsible partner/interagency source.
Requires holding or revising unsupported commitments.
Includes protection reassessment for changed threat behaviour.
Preserves existing authority conditions.
Preserves mission/force-expansion reporting requirements.

acceptable_alternatives: A branch-planning and decision-gate process is acceptable; immediate wholesale mission termination is not mandatory.
error_conditions: Unilaterally takes Japanese enforcement or response-lead functions.
questions.derivation_note: Maps conditional mission feasibility to a concrete revalidation and task-adjustment process.

questions.title: Coordination-change trigger
questions.question: What coordination provision follows from the conditional status of OCHA participation?
questions.expected_answer: Use the current bilateral/Japanese-led arrangement as the working baseline, monitor any Japanese decision to internationalise the appeal, and prepare to update liaison and reporting interfaces if that trigger occurs. Retain validated-gap and Japanese-lead requirements.

criteria.text: States the current coordination baseline without making it permanent.
Names the Japanese internationalisation decision as the trigger.
Requires updating the liaison/reporting interfaces if the trigger occurs.
Preserves Japanese leadership under the revised coordination arrangement.
Preserves the validated-gap requirement under the revised coordination arrangement.

acceptable_alternatives: A time-bounded assumption with an explicit review trigger and interface action is acceptable.
error_conditions: Establishes active OCHA clusters without the stated condition.
questions.derivation_note: Provides a concrete coordination-change provision from the temporal assessment.

questions.title: Expansion request control
questions.question: What prerequisite should govern a proposed relief package outside the currently requested capability set or force scale?
questions.expected_answer: Document the validated gap with Japan and USAID/BHA, identify the additional capability and support it requires, and route the expansion through COMUSFJ/bilateral and US command reporting for the required decision. Keep the new commitment conditional until authority, allocation and sustainment are confirmed.

criteria.text: Requires validation of the additional gap.
Identifies the additional capability required.
Identifies the additional sustainment required by the expanded package.
Identifies the additional force support required by the expanded package.
Routes expansion through established coordination/reporting.
Keeps expansion conditional on confirmed authority.
Keeps expansion conditional on actual force allocation.
Keeps expansion conditional on confirmed sustainment support.

acceptable_alternatives: A decision request or change-control entry is acceptable.
error_conditions: Assumes the original diplomatic request approves unlimited expansion.
questions.derivation_note: Combines a bounded request, command channels and limited sustainment into an explicit commitment prerequisite.

dependencies.counterfactual_test: If current clearance and relevant site support are verified for a particular aircraft and delivery task, nominal runway data no longer leave that task's access unresolved. Fixed-wing clearance alone must not remove the separate rotary/VTOL suitability gap.

dependencies.rationale: The assessed dependency identifies the specific requirement to resolve before the staff decision.
dependencies.counterfactual_test: If the responsible authorities already provide a current, task-matched rotary/VTOL suitability and support report, do not request redundant verification as if access were unknown. If a site is unusable, restrict or redirect that delivery rather than infer clearance from runway length.

dependencies.counterfactual_test: If usable, accessible satellite endpoints and local power are confirmed at the affected island, the assigned space-support task can be linked to a demonstrated service. An assignment without those confirmations still does not establish island connectivity.

dependencies.rationale: The assessed dependency identifies the specific requirement to resolve before the staff decision.
dependencies.counterfactual_test: If current checks establish usable terminals, power and interoperability at an island, close the corresponding gap rather than request new equipment automatically. If one prerequisite fails, target the support adjustment to that failed function.

dependencies.counterfactual_test: If the intended audience has verified access to a working channel, the specific delivery uncertainty is reduced. Improved connectivity alone does not replace the separate message and employment approvals.

dependencies.counterfactual_test: If current station status, frequencies and access establish a usable authorized radio channel, further radio discovery is unnecessary for that channel. chains.title: Shared force to readiness and comparison

dependencies.rationale: A finite force pool, standing commitments and allocation responsibilities jointly define the resource trade.
dependencies.counterfactual_test: If a separately allocated replacement provides the standing afloat crisis-response function during the relief commitment, the sole-force opportunity cost changes. Merely listing a second planning asset without timely allocation does not remove the trade.

dependencies.rationale: The assessment identifies the readiness or commitment issue; A004 supplies the actual command/allocation channel required for the follow-up decision.
dependencies.counterfactual_test: If current readiness and availability demonstrate that the approved relief commitment leaves the standing response requirement covered, no conflict-based reallocation request follows. If coverage is lost, refer that documented conflict through the designated command allocation process.

dependencies.counterfactual_test: If competing packages leave different verified standing-mission coverage, the comparison must reflect that difference. If their coverage is genuinely identical, this criterion should not create a fictitious readiness advantage for one package.

chains.minimality_note: A004 supplies command/allocation responsibility directly to the F task. It is not a necessary premise for the underlying resource or assumption judgement. Source access remains available.

dependencies.rationale: LOTS support depends jointly on the physical window and confirmed resources.
dependencies.counterfactual_test: If connector capability, allocated sustainment and a suitable weather/tidal window are all confirmed, the present uncertainty about that LOTS period is reduced. Improvement in sea state alone cannot make pending vessels or support available.

dependencies.rationale: The assessed dependency identifies the specific requirement to resolve before the staff decision.

If the window closes or capacity falls short, revise timing, mode or support against the actual deficit.

chains.title: Expansion to sustainment test

dependencies.rationale: Validated additional demand must be matched to confirmed support and the bounded authority to expand.
dependencies.counterfactual_test: If the proposed package remains within the confirmed initial sustainment basis and requested scope, the expansion-specific support gap does not arise. A larger package still needs demand and support confirmation even when ACSA exists.

dependencies.rationale: The assessed dependency identifies the specific requirement to resolve before the staff decision.
dependencies.counterfactual_test: If confirmed support meets the package's demand for its full duration, record that adequacy rather than a dependence on pending augmentation. If scale or duration rises beyond support, the comparison must expose the newly uncovered requirement.

dependencies.rationale: The assessed dependency identifies the specific requirement to resolve before the staff decision.
dependencies.counterfactual_test: If the requested package fits the existing validated gap, authority, allocation and sustainment, an expansion request is unnecessary. If any requested scale or capability exceeds those bounds, keep only that extension pending while the responsible authorities decide it.

chains.chain_rationale: Validated additional demand must be matched to confirmed support and the bounded authority to expand.
chains.minimality_note: The listed inputs are jointly used for this bounded judgement. Source access remains available, so graph membership is not proof of model use.

chains.title: Transport path to delivered-relief criterion

dependencies.rationale: Mission purpose, infrastructure/service dependencies and the supplied transport posture distinguish arrival at a staging or entry point from usable relief at the destination.
dependencies.counterfactual_test: If onward handling and distribution are restored and intended recipients receive usable supplies on time, the particular gap between staging and effective relief narrows. Faster dispatch alone does not establish delivery while a downstream service remains unavailable.

dependencies.rationale: The assessed dependency identifies the specific requirement to resolve before the staff decision.
dependencies.counterfactual_test: If two options dispatch at the same time but one reaches intended recipients later because of a verified handling bottleneck, the timely-relief comparison must distinguish them. If delivery and usability are equivalent, staging differences alone must not create an unsupported advantage.

chains.chain_rationale: A001 supplies the purpose, A006 supplies the service/distribution dependencies and A011 supplies the transport stages. The historical event and distance inventories are not necessary analytical premises.
chains.minimality_note: The event/date inventory and exact distances were removed as background. Airhead conditions are represented by A011 here and are evaluated more specifically through A008 in CH001. Full original sources remain available.

chains.title: MDA support to approval gate

dependencies.rationale: The support boundary and uncertain anomaly picture constrain the timing and permitted form of response.
dependencies.counterfactual_test: If both the JCG request and State concurrence cover the proposed support, that authority dependency is resolved subject to actual resources and timing. Confirmed sensors or stronger diversion reporting alone cannot substitute for either approval.

dependencies.rationale: The assessed dependency identifies the specific requirement to resolve before the staff decision.
dependencies.counterfactual_test: If both approvals arrive within the intended window and the resources remain available, no approval-driven rescheduling follows. If approval arrives after that window or assets become unavailable, revalidate the window and resource commitment while preserving Japanese enforcement responsibility.

chains.chain_rationale: The support boundary and uncertain anomaly picture constrain the timing and permitted form of response.

chains.title: Unverified discrepancy to verification task

dependencies.rationale: The supplied distribution dependencies, uncertain criminal picture, alternative hypotheses and actual discrepancies limit what can be concluded about diversion. A conditional COG label adds no necessary premise.
dependencies.counterfactual_test: If matched records resolve the discrepancy as recording lag or storm loss, the case for criminal diversion is not sustained by that anomaly. If an unexplained residual remains, it still needs corroboration before a diversion location, amount or connected network is asserted.

dependencies.rationale: The unresolved-discrepancy assessment defines the verification task, while A014 determines the Japanese authority and referral boundary for any criminal finding.
dependencies.counterfactual_test: If reconciliation explains the missing receipt, correct the logistics record rather than refer it as confirmed criminal diversion. notes: All references describe a synthetic training scenario. The scenario legal statements are not asserted as current real-world legal advice.
The source packet supplies no numerical platform throughput, safe operating thresholds, active radio frequencies or verified satellite-terminal inventory. Criteria do not invent these values.
C10-GAP-06 is retained with explicit source-stated-gap status and a newly constructed verification task. C10-GAP-10 is bounded by the actual conditional OCHA statement.
All 47 accepted positive items have been inspected. Source-stated actions remain A; derived B/F outputs are distinct consequences. New constructions await military-expert validation.

Independent construction review clarified B001 scope, made F010 approval-delay consequences concrete, kept F011 unresolved losses distinct from corroborated diversion, and qualified F008 continuity by existing authority.

Independent minimality review removed historical-event, distance and conditional-COG nodes that had no substantive chain role. S10-01 is partially reused only for infrastructure damage. Command/authority parents were moved to the F tasks they actually constrain. Independent factual and decision conditions were split into atomic scoring entries.

Final criterion atomicity review split independent enumerated capabilities, approval conditions and requested facts without changing question wording, references or graph membership. Genuine relational comparisons remain intact.

Final dependency review replaced generic counterfactual wording with scenario-specific qualitative checks. These are unexecuted construction annotations for expert review, not empirical intervention results.
